blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Loft Conversion Cost in Crawley in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: Find out how much a loft conversion costs in Crawley in 2026. We break down the different conversion types, local pricing factors, and what to expect from your project.
body: A loft conversion is one of the most popular home improvement projects for homeowners in Crawley, and for good reason. With property prices continuing to rise across West Sussex, adding usable living space to your existing home is a smart investment. But how much does a loft conversion actually cost in Crawley in 2026? The answer depends on several factors, including the type of conversion, the size and shape of your roof, and the level of finish you require. At True Grain Carpentry, we have completed numerous loft conversions across Crawley and the surrounding Surrey-Sussex area, giving us an in-depth understanding of local pricing.

There are several types of loft conversions available to Crawley homeowners, each with different cost implications. A simple Velux roof window conversion, which does not require changes to the roof structure, typically represents the most affordable option. A dormer loft conversion, which extends the roof to create additional headroom and floor space, is the most common choice in Crawley due to the town's predominantly terraced and semi-detached housing stock. Hip-to-gable conversions are popular on detached and semi-detached properties in areas like Northgate and Three Bridges, while mansard conversions offer maximum space but come at a higher cost due to the extensive structural work involved.

When budgeting for a loft conversion in Crawley, you should expect to pay between £30,000 and £70,000 depending on the type and specification. A basic Velux conversion may start from around £30,000 to £35,000, while a standard rear dormer conversion typically ranges from £40,000 to £55,000. For more complex projects such as hip-to-gable or mansard conversions, costs can rise to £55,000 to £70,000 or more. These prices usually include structural work, insulation, plumbing for an en-suite, plastering, and electrical work. At True Grain Carpentry, we provide detailed, transparent quotes that break down every element of the project so you know exactly where your money is going.

Crawley presents some unique considerations for loft conversions. Many properties in the town centre and older neighbourhoods like Pound Hill and Ifield were built between the 1950s and 1970s, with roof structures that may need additional support for a conversion. Newer developments in Bewbush, Broadfield, and West Green often have more straightforward roof designs but may be subject to different building regulation requirements. The proximity of properties in residential areas also means that party wall agreements may be needed, which can add to both the timeline and cost of your project. Our team at True Grain Carpentry has extensive experience navigating these local requirements.

Most loft conversions in Crawley fall under permitted development rights, meaning you will not need full planning permission. However, there are exceptions, particularly for properties in conservation areas, listed buildings, or flats. Crawley has several conservation areas, and if your property is within one, you may need to submit a planning application. Regardless of whether planning permission is required, all loft conversions must comply with Building Regulations, which cover structural integrity, fire safety, insulation, and ventilation. True Grain Carpentry works closely with building control officers throughout the Crawley area to ensure every project meets current standards.

If you are considering a loft conversion in Crawley, Horsham, or anywhere across Surrey and Sussex, True Grain Carpentry can help. We offer free, detailed quotes with no obligation, and our team will advise you on the best type of conversion for your property and budget. With our commitment to quality craftsmanship and transparent pricing, we have built a reputation as one of the most trusted carpentry businesses in the Crawley area. Get in touch today to discuss your loft conversion project and discover how we can add valuable living space to your home.

blogPosts.title: Bespoke Kitchen Worktops and Cabinets: A Guide for Crawley Homeowners
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover the benefits of bespoke kitchen worktops and cabinets for your Crawley home. A complete guide to materials, costs, and the craftsmanship that makes the difference.
body: A bespoke kitchen is the heart of any home, and for homeowners in Crawley, investing in custom-designed worktops and cabinets is a decision that adds both value and character to your property. Unlike off-the-shelf kitchen solutions, bespoke carpentry allows you to create a space that perfectly fits your lifestyle, from the grain of the timber to the style of the handles. At True Grain Carpentry, we specialise in designing and crafting bespoke kitchen furniture for homes across Crawley and the wider West Sussex area, combining traditional joinery techniques with modern precision to deliver kitchens that are truly one of a kind.

One of the biggest decisions when commissioning a bespoke kitchen in Crawley is choosing the right materials. Solid hardwoods such as oak, walnut, and maple remain popular choices for worktops and cabinets, offering warmth, durability, and a timeless aesthetic. Oak is particularly favoured by Crawley homeowners for its versatility and resistance to daily wear, while walnut provides a rich, dark contrast that suits contemporary kitchen designs. For worktops, engineered options like quartz offer low-maintenance alternatives, though many clients prefer the natural beauty of timber. At True Grain Carpentry, we source quality timbers and can guide you through the selection process.

Designing a bespoke kitchen requires careful consideration of your available space, cooking habits, and aesthetic preferences. In Crawley, kitchen layouts vary widely from compact galley kitchens in terraced houses to expansive open-plan spaces in newer detached homes. Our design process at True Grain Carpentry begins with a thorough consultation at your Crawley property, where we measure your space, discuss your requirements, and explore design options. We pay particular attention to the workflow between sink, cooker, and storage areas, ensuring your new kitchen is not only beautiful but also highly functional. Every cabinet and worktop is crafted to precise measurements for a seamless fit.

There is a noticeable difference between factory-produced kitchen units and handcrafted bespoke furniture. At True Grain Carpentry, every cabinet is constructed using traditional joinery methods, including dovetail joints and mortise-and-tenon connections, which provide superior strength and longevity compared to mass-produced alternatives. Our worktops are hand-finished to bring out the natural beauty of the timber, and each piece is treated with food-safe finishes that protect against moisture and heat. For Crawley homeowners who value quality over compromise, a bespoke kitchen from True Grain represents an investment that will serve your family for decades to come.

Bespoke kitchen worktops and cabinets in Crawley typically range from £5,000 to £25,000 or more, depending on the size of the kitchen, the materials selected, and the complexity of the design. Solid oak worktops generally cost between £80 and £150 per square metre, while walnut can range from £120 to £200 per square metre. Handcrafted cabinets typically start from £500 per unit for simple designs, rising to £1,500 or more for intricate, fully custom pieces. At True Grain Carpentry, we provide detailed quotes that break down material costs, labour, and finishing, ensuring complete transparency before any work begins.

Ready to transform your Crawley kitchen with bespoke worktops and cabinets? True Grain Carpentry offers free, no-obligation consultations and detailed quotes tailored to your specific project. Whether you are planning a complete kitchen refit or simply want to replace worktops and cabinetry, our team has the skills and experience to bring your vision to life. Contact us today to arrange a visit at your Crawley home and discover the difference that genuine craftsmanship can make.

blogPosts.title: Traditional Green Oak Framing in Sussex: Costs, Benefits and What to Expect
blogPosts.excerpt: Learn about traditional green oak framing in Sussex, including costs, benefits, and what self-builders in Crawley should know before commissioning an oak-framed structure.
body: Traditional green oak framing is a craft that has defined the architectural character of Sussex for centuries, from medieval halls and tithe barns to modern country homes. For homeowners and self-builders in Crawley and across West Sussex, commissioning a green oak frame offers the opportunity to create a structure that is not only beautiful and enduring but also deeply rooted in the local building heritage. True Grain Carpentry is one of the few specialist carpentry businesses in the Crawley area with the expertise to design, craft, and erect traditional green oak frames, making us your ideal partner for this distinctive building method.

Green oak framing uses freshly felled oak that has not been seasoned or dried, typically containing around 60 to 80 percent moisture content. The term 'green' refers to this unseasoned state, and it is this quality that gives the technique its unique characteristics. As the oak dries naturally over the first few years after installation, it shrinks slightly, causing the joints to tighten and the frame to become increasingly rigid. This natural process, combined with the high tannin content of English oak, creates structures of remarkable strength and durability. A well-built green oak frame can last for centuries, as evidenced by surviving examples across the Sussex countryside.

In the Crawley area, green oak framing is used for a variety of projects, from full structural frames for new builds and extensions to decorative garden structures, pergolas, and porch canopies. Many self-builders in the villages surrounding Crawley, including Ifield, Pease Pottage, and Copthorne, choose green oak framing to create homes with character and authenticity. The frames can be left exposed internally to showcase the beauty of the oak, creating stunning vaulted ceilings and exposed beam work. At True Grain Carpentry, we have worked on projects ranging from small garden arbours to full two-storey oak-framed extensions, tailoring each design to the specific needs of the property.

The cost of traditional green oak framing varies significantly depending on the scale and complexity of the project. For a simple garden structure such as a pergola or porch, prices typically start from around £3,000 to £8,000. A full oak-framed extension or small new-build shell in the Crawley area generally costs between £25,000 and £60,000, depending on the size and design. The price of green oak timber itself fluctuates but typically ranges from £800 to £1,400 per cubic metre for quality English green oak. Additional costs include design fees, crane hire for erection, and the specialist skills required for traditional joinery. At True Grain Carpentry, we provide comprehensive quotes covering every aspect of your oak framing project.

There are many reasons why homeowners in Crawley and West Sussex choose green oak framing over conventional construction methods. The aesthetic appeal is perhaps the most obvious benefit, with the warm tones and natural grain of oak creating a living space of extraordinary beauty. However, the practical advantages are equally compelling. Green oak frames are incredibly strong and can span large distances without the need for internal supports, creating open, light-filled spaces. The natural insulating properties of timber help regulate temperature, and as the oak weathers over time, it develops a distinctive silver-grey patina that blends beautifully with the Sussex landscape.

If you are interested in traditional green oak framing for your next project in Crawley, Horsham, or anywhere across Surrey and Sussex, True Grain Carpentry would be delighted to discuss your ideas. We offer initial consultations at your property or in our workshop, where you can see examples of our work and explore the possibilities for your project. From initial design through to final erection, our specialist team handles every detail. Contact us today for a free, no-obligation quote.

blogPosts.title: Restoring Historic Barns and Oast Houses in West Sussex
blogPosts.excerpt: A guide to restoring historic barns and oast houses in West Sussex. Learn about planning requirements, traditional techniques, and costs for Crawley and Sussex property owners.
body: West Sussex is home to an extraordinary wealth of historic agricultural buildings, from sprawling threshing barns to the iconic conical oast houses that once served the region's thriving hop industry. For property owners who have acquired these characterful buildings, restoration represents both a privilege and a challenge. True Grain Carpentry, based in Crawley, has established a reputation as one of the leading specialists in historic building restoration across the Surrey and Sussex area, with particular expertise in barn conversions, oast house repairs, and the sympathetic repair of traditional timber frames that define the region's architectural heritage.

Restoring a historic barn or oast house presents unique challenges that require specialist knowledge and experience. Many of these buildings are structurally complex, with massive timber frames that may have shifted or deteriorated over centuries. Common issues include rot in the sole plates and base of posts, insect damage to structural timbers, and the failure of traditional lime mortar joints. In the Crawley area, where clay soils can cause significant movement, foundation issues are also common in older buildings. True Grain Carpentry's team understands these challenges intimately, drawing on extensive experience to diagnose problems accurately and implement repairs that respect the original construction methods.

Many historic barns and oast houses in the West Sussex area are listed buildings, which means that any alterations or repairs require consent from the local planning authority. In the Crawley and Mid Sussex district, listed building consent is a legal requirement for works that affect the character of a listed structure. This can include everything from replacing damaged timbers to altering openings or adding modern services. True Grain Carpentry works closely with planning officers and conservation specialists to ensure that all restoration work complies with the requirements of the Planning Listed Buildings and Conservation Areas Act, while still achieving the functional outcomes you need.

At True Grain Carpentry, we believe that authentic restoration demands the use of traditional materials and techniques wherever possible. This means using green oak or Douglas fir to match original timbers, employing traditional mortise-and-tenon joinery secured with wooden pegs, and applying lime mortar rather than modern cement-based products. Lime mortar is essential in historic buildings because it allows the structure to breathe, preventing moisture buildup that can cause timber decay. For oast house restoration, we have specialist knowledge of the unique construction methods used in these buildings, including the curved internal walls and the distinctive conical roofs that make oast houses so recognisable across the Sussex landscape.

The cost of restoring a historic barn or oast house in the Crawley area varies enormously depending on the extent of the work required. Minor repairs to a timber frame might cost between £5,000 and £15,000, while a full barn conversion with modern services, insulation, and internal fit-out could range from £100,000 to £250,000 or more. Oast house restorations are typically among the most complex and costly projects due to their unique geometry and the specialist skills required. At True Grain Carpentry, we provide detailed assessments and realistic quotes before any work begins, ensuring you have a clear understanding of the investment required for your restoration project.

If you own a historic barn, oast house, or period property in Crawley, Horsham, or across West Sussex and are considering restoration, True Grain Carpentry can help. Our specialist team has the knowledge, skills, and passion to breathe new life into these remarkable buildings while preserving their character and heritage. We offer free initial consultations and detailed assessments, working with you to develop a restoration plan that meets your needs and respects the building's history. Get in touch today to discuss your historic building project and discover why property owners across Surrey and Sussex trust True Grain Carpentry with their most valued structures.
